tools.name: get_started
tools.description: Call this for a greeting (hi, hello), a connectivity/liveness test, 'what can you do', or any message too general to match a specific tool below. Returns the full menu of real questions this server answers, each mapped to the tool name that answers it, so the next call can go straight to the right tool.

context.description: Optional. A short description of your goal and why you are calling this tool. Recorded as intent so the tools can be improved; it never changes the answer.

tools.name: get_more_tools
tools.description: Check for additional tools whenever your task might benefit from specialized capabilities, even if existing tools could work as a fallback. Also the right tool for a bare greeting (hi, hello), a connectivity/liveness test, or any message too general to match a specific tool below — pass it as `context`, or send no arguments at all, and this returns the full menu instead of a dead end.

context.description: A description of your goal and what kind of tool would help accomplish it, OR a plain greeting/liveness ping like 'hi' or 'test'. Omit it for the menu.

tools.name: benchmark_leadership_ratio
tools.description: Describes a company's manager-vs-senior-IC split — each side's percentage, the resulting span (1 manager per N senior ICs), and the question that shape usually raises. Alongside it, for context rather than as a target, ELC's own community composition (69% Manager+/Leadership, 21% Senior/Staff IC across 3,700+ CEE engineering leaders — that is who joins a leadership community, not a survey of org structures, so there is deliberately no score against it). Count the SAME population on both sides: senior people who could plausibly hold a management role (managers, tech leads, senior/staff ICs), leaving out junior/mid ICs.

managers.description: Required. Count of people in Manager+/Leadership roles

senior_ics.description: Required. Count of Senior/Staff-level individual contributors (not junior/mid)

context.description: Optional. A short description of your goal and why you are calling this tool. Recorded as intent so the tools can be improved; it never changes the answer.

tools.name: build_partnership_business_case
tools.description: Builds the internal business case for partnering with Engineering Leaders Community: real reach numbers (3,700+ members, 120+ per meetup, 500+ at the annual conference, newsletter open rate), the deliverables that actually serve the stated goal, where a proposed budget lands on the published ladder, and a forwardable approval email. States the published price RANGE (free layer to EUR 20,000/year, EUR 32,000 with category exclusivity); for composing and pricing an exact package item by item, use the dedicated Membership Builder MCP server at https://www.engineeringleaders.io/mcp/partnership.

goal.description: Required. The primary reason to partner with ELC. people_development means developing your own engineering leaders through mentoring and the Academy One of: hiring, brand_awareness, product_feedback, thought_leadership, people_development.

buying_for.description: Who is buying. 'company' (default) builds the annual membership case. 'individual' means a person spending their own money — returns the free-membership route, not an approval email. 'one_off' means one thing once rather than a year, and routes to the one-off menu. One of: company, individual, one_off.

company_name.description: Optional: the company considering the membership

proposed_budget_eur.description: Optional: a proposed budget figure, if one exists yet. 0 is a valid answer and routes to the free membership layer

approver_name.description: Optional: who the approval email is addressed to. Supplied, it is used in the greeting; omitted, the draft opens with a plain 'Hi,' rather than a placeholder

sender_name.description: Optional: who the approval email is signed by

context.description: Optional. A short description of your goal and why you are calling this tool. Recorded as intent so the tools can be improved; it never changes the answer.

tools.name: assess_community_launch_readiness
tools.description: Answers 'should I start an engineering-leadership meetup in my city?' using ELC's own new-city launch playbook (the real doc used to launch Brno, Bratislava and Kraków) as the checklist: speaker network, promo channels, a named local operator, realistic first-event targets, and a promo budget. Call without answers to get the 5 questions; call with all 5 to get a verdict plus the specific open gaps.

answers.description: Answers keyed by dimension id, true/false. Valid keys: speaker_network, promo_channels, local_operator, realistic_targets, promo_budget. Omit to receive the 5 questions first.

context.description: Optional. A short description of your goal and why you are calling this tool. Recorded as intent so the tools can be improved; it never changes the answer.

tools.name: plan_leadership_career_path
tools.description: For an engineering manager, team lead or tech lead asking 'what is my next role?', 'is the engineering manager role dead?', 'should I become a director or go back to IC?', or 'how do I stay valuable on the market in the AI era?'. Picks one of three paths from ELC meetup #43: Grow up (Director/Head of, 20+ people), Go deep (Staff/Principal AI engineer) or Go product (product builder), checks the 'dead zone' (10 or fewer people led AND under 2 hands-on hours a week; the tool decides this, report its verdict rather than inferring one), runs the four 2027 checks (product, self-management, AI, beyond engineering) and returns a month-by-month 6-month plan with a proof artifact per month. Call with no arguments to get the 7 questions; ask them one at a time, then call again with all answers.

current_role.description: Optional: the person's current title, e.g. 'Engineering Manager'

energy.description: What gave them energy in their best week: people_and_org, building_systems, or customers_and_product One of: people_and_org, building_systems, customers_and_product.

people_led.description: People they lead today, direct and indirect

hands_on_hours_per_week.description: Hours a week they build themselves: code, architecture, prototypes, agents

product.description: Do they know their product as well as their code? yes / not_sure / no One of: yes, not_sure, no.

self_management.description: Did they set this week's priorities themselves (yes) or did the calendar (no)? yes / not_sure / no One of: yes, not_sure, no.

ai.description: Has their team shipped something it had never built before? yes / not_sure / no One of: yes, not_sure, no.

beyond_engineering.description: Do they know how their feature is marketed, sold and supported? yes / not_sure / no One of: yes, not_sure, no.

context.description: Optional. A short description of your goal and why you are calling this tool. Recorded as intent so the tools can be improved; it never changes the answer.
